questions.question: When inspecting a tank, a driver should:

options.text: Look online for information about the vehicle.
Make sure there is no rust on the outside of the tank.

questions.explanation: Each tank type has different features. Always check your vehicle's operator manual to learn how to inspect your specific tank.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, the driver should:
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the truck.

questions.question: Placarded vehicles must carry fire extinguishers with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: Placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle, which of the following should not cause concern?

options.text: Exhaust system parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are leaking
Exhaust system parts made of aluminum

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts made of aluminum
questions.explanation: Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts; damaged brackets or clamps; parts rubbing against fuel or other systems; and leaks. The material of the exhaust parts is not a concern.

questions.question: Starting in which year were newly manufactured trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum leakage rate is 3 psi per minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good rule to follow when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get the attention of other drivers.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal early and well in advance of your turn. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: When making tight maneuvers, you should:

options.text: Open your door for a better look.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently as part of your normal scanning routine. This is especially important when driving in tight spaces.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is controlled by the brake pedal. It applies and releases the brakes during normal driving.

questions.question: Regarding winter driving, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Front tires should have a tread depth of at least 4/32 an inch.
Rear tires should have a tread depth of at least 2/32 an inch.
Use a gauge to verify that each tire has a safe tread depth.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread for safety. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check tread depths. Do not deflate your tires.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a single vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, air should leak no more than 2 psi per minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Turns on the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Keeps the spring brakes in place until they are needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main air tank. It stops air from leaking out of the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: What should you pay extra attention to during a winter pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: In winter, make sure your coolant and antifreeze levels are safe. This is especially important to prevent engine freezing.

questions.question: On a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third when driving on wet roads. Slippery surfaces make it harder to stop and turn, so slower speeds are needed for safe driving.

questions.question: If you don't know how to put out a fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are unsure how to put out a fire, wait for firefighters to arrive. Let them handle it. This is very important, especially with fires involving dangerous materials.

questions.question: If a trailer's spring brakes don't release when you push the tractor air supply control, what should you do?
questions.explanation: All vehicle equipment must work properly before you drive. If the trailer's spring brakes don't release, check that all air line connections are properly attached and sealed.

questions.question: What does a "Maximum Safe Speed" sign mean?

options.text: It is a suggestion. Vehicles may travel faster than the posted speed.
It only applies to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
You must follow it. No vehicle should go faster than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow it. No vehicle should go faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: You must never drive faster than the speed shown on a "Maximum Safe Speed" sign.

questions.question: In an emergency, if you must drive onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Steer so all wheels are on the shoulder.
Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must drive onto the shoulder, keep one set of wheels on the pavement to stay in better control. If possible, stop completely on the shoulder before pulling back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after rain begins?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil from cars that has not yet washed away. This creates a slippery and dangerous surface.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.
